Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Wheeze and SOB x2–3 days

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has had wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: CC: Wheeze and SOB x2–3 days

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reported feeling feverish but self-checked temperature was 37
Patient has shortness of breath on exertion but none at rest
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: SOB on exertion, none at rest

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Sometimes it is hard for the patient to finish sentences
Symptoms have not woken the patient at night
Patient reports being unable to exercise due to symptoms
At the time of note, patient reports currently feeling well
Patient does not have a peak flow meter at home
Patient does not have a spacer device

Past_Medical_History.content: History of childhood asthma described as quite bad
Intermittent hospital visits for asthma as a child
Past_Medical_History.source_text: intermittent hospital visits for asthma as child

Past_Medical_History.content: No history of ICU admission for asthma
Asthma caused the patient to miss school in childhood
Patient reports stopping asthma medications approximately 3–4 years ago
Patient later reports using salbutamol inhaler as needed every few weeks and before exercise
Past_Medical_History.source_text: later reports using salbutamol inhaler PRN every few weeks and before exercise

Medications.content: Current medication: salbutamol inhaler as needed
Patient is on no other regular medications

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks approximately one glass of wine every 2–3 days
Patient is working from home or on sick leave due to shortness of breath
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: working from home/sick leave due to SOB

Assessment.source_text: 1) Asthma exacerbation — 2–3 d wheeze/SOB with exertional limitation; cough without sputum; no CP/hemoptysis; not nocturnal; no rest dyspnea; no spacer/PEF device; atopic history

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase short-acting beta agonist: salbutamol 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Increase SABA: Salbutamol 2–4 puffs q4h initially

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe spacer and have pharmacist demonstrate its use
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Rx spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate use

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe peak flow meter and have pharmacist teach technique
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Rx peak flow meter; pharmacist to teach technique

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to record peak expiratory flow twice daily in the morning and evening for one week
Arrange phone review after one week of PEF recordings to assess need for additional inhaler
Plan_of_Care.source_text: phone review to assess need for additional inhaler

Plan_of_Care.content: Start regular over-the-counter antihistamine with pharmacy advice
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Start regular OTC antihistamine (pharmacy advice per note)

Plan_of_Care.content: Safety-net advice: call back urgently if high temperature develops or wheeze worsens
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety-net: call back urgently if high temperature or worsening wheeze

Follow_up_Information.content: Arrange asthma review in approximately one week, earlier if deterioration
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Arrange asthma review in ~1 week (earlier if deterioration)

Review_of_Systems.content: Respiratory review positive for wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days
Review_of_Systems.source_text: CC: Wheeze and SOB x2–3 days

Review_of_Systems.content: Respiratory review positive for cough without sputum
Respiratory review negative for chest pain
Respiratory review negative for nocturnal symptoms
